label: Martina Franca

names.text: "Asino di Martina Franca" taken from the Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch, where it is given as the Italian name. The intake's "Asino Martinese" is not confirmed by the article or by any page opened, so it is left out.

about.text: The donkey breed of Puglia in southern Italy, named after the town of Martina Franca. Its historical main use was producing mules; since the 1990s, demand for donkey meat and asses' milk has created new uses for it.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the origin in Puglia and the town, the mule history, and the new demand for meat and asses' milk since the 1990s.

origin.place: Puglia, southern Italy; named after the comune of Martina Franca, with an area of origin that also includes Alberobello, Ceglie Messapica, Locorotondo, Massafra, Mottola and Noci.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the comune and the area of origin. The article gives no date of origin, so none is used.

Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: listed uses are siring mules, burden, light draught, meat and milk; donkey meat and asses' milk have created new demand since the 1990s. The order puts meat and milk first, following that recent demand.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the FAO listed the breed as "endangered" in 2007. No current DAD-IS status was found.

facts.v: In 1925, 70% of Italian mules were produced in Puglia. Exports of the donkey were restricted from 1926 because of strong foreign demand, and the mules were widely used in the First World War.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the 1925 share of Italian mules, the 1926 export restriction, and the use in the First World War.

gaps: No population count for the breed in 2008 beyond the article's "just under 400", so no head figure is given; no milk composition or yield figures (the article gives none, and the study figures found in search text were not opened); no DAD-IS status; no formation year for the breed (the article gives a herdbook of 1943 and a breeders' association of 1948, which are not the breed's origin).
